steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: Morning, Hung. Day off?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Hehe, something came up, so I had to call out.

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: Are you sick? You should go home and rest!

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Nah, it's not that.

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: So, how's your new job going?

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: (Whisper) Shh! That look on his face, I bet he got fired again.

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: (Whisper) Again? How many times has that been...? Kid's too nice and doesn't know how to be flexible.

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: (Whisper) You've got to be clever to make it these days.

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: (Whisper) Yeah, got to move with the times.

steps.name: Former Boss
steps.text: What did I tell you when you first showed up? Don't poke your nose where it doesn't belong!

steps.name: Former Boss
steps.text: Looks like you spent so much time at the top that your brain got addled from the lack of oxygen.

steps.name: Former Boss
steps.text: You gotta be flexible if you wanna do business in Lungmen!

steps.name: Former Boss
steps.text: You have any idea how much work it took to get this batch of goods?

steps.name: Former Boss
steps.text: And you threw it all out, just because you weren't sure of the source! Thank you very much, Mister Avatar of Justice!

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Boss, this stuff's dangerous... what if it gets into the hands of the mafia?

steps.name: Former Boss
steps.text: Who cares as long as they pay in gold and silver? Who do you think you are, trying to teach me how to do business?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Former Boss
steps.text: But what? No buts. Get out, and don't let me see your face again.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Sorry, boss, I just...

steps.name: Former Boss
steps.text: Get out! You're just like your dad. He deserved to be broke, and you deserve to be out on the street!

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Boss, this has nothing to do with my dad...

steps.name: Former Boss
steps.text: GET LOST!

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Rumble—)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Sigh... I should get something to eat, then I can think about what to do next.)

steps.name: Street Ad
steps.text: Grand opening! 20% off during the opening promotion! Don't miss your chance to taste authentic Shangshu home cooking!

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Reaches for the wallet)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: I think I have enough. Let's go.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Welcome! What can I get you?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Er, let me look at the menu.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: How about our signature item the 'Full House?' A set of meat and vegetable toppings. It's really great!

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Thanks, but I'll just have a bowl of plain noodles.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Just plain noodles? No drink, no sides?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: No, thanks. Just plain noodles.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Hmph. Fine, take a number and get in line.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: ...Thanks.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I'm looking to get a small bowl of noodles... any recommendations for a first timer?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: That would be our signature 'Full House.' Everyone loves it!

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Sure, I'll take it.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Now that's what I like to hear. Here's your number, and I'll have it to you in a jiffy.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Alright then, thanks.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hey, buddy, have you eaten here before? What do you think?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: No, this is my first time.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Ever had Shangshu food before?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: I had some when I was little, at a big restaurant with my dad. I loved it.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Haha. Bigger isn't always better when it comes to restaurants.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Here's your noodles, sir. Would love to hear your thoughts afterwards, good or bad.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Sure thing.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Excuse me, what about mine...?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: You can't rush things, you know. Noodles take time.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: But this gentleman's are ready. Why are mine taking longer?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: What are you talking about? You didn't order the same type.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Young people these days have no patience. Good food takes time!

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Ahem. Probably shouldn't keep your customers waiting, friend. You just opened, after all.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Huh? Oh, yeah, you're right, enjoy your meal.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Nods in gratitude)

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Haha, don't mention it.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (I guess I can wait a little longer.)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (The interior of this place looks pretty nice. I guess this is the Shangshu style.)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (When I was little, dad said we would go to Shangshu and really dig into the local cuisine... bah, no use thinking about it when he's not around anymore.)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Hey, why is that guy peeking left and right?)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (He took out a paper packet... Wait, did he just pinch something into the bowl?)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Hey, what are you doi—

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: Hey, boss, what's going on here?!

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Is there a problem, sir?

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: There's a bug in this bowl! Look, a huge one, black and shiny.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: That's impossible. I hold myself to the highest standard of cleanliness.

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: Talk all you want! I got proof floating right there in this bowl!

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: What are you trying to pull?! I've got cameras watching the shop, they'll prove you're just looking for trouble.

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: (Flips over the table) Huh? You want a fight?
Busy with their argument, neither party notices that the bowl of noodles, which was launched into the air with the table, is headed straight for Lee.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: (No rush. I can dodge it after another bite.)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Ow, it burns!

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Are you ok, sir? Did any of the soup hit you?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I'm fine. You got a faceful of the hot noodle soup, though. Here, use this handkerchief.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: (Ack, I guess I owe him one now.)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Thank you.
Hung shakes off the pieces of noodles and vegetables on his face, then wipes it with the handkerchief.
He holds the soiled cloth in his hand, not sure what to do. He looks over to Lee, seeing him point to the top of his head.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: There's still something there.
Hung scratches his head, feels something hard in the fur, and pulls out a big, black, shiny bug.

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: You want a beating, huh?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: H-Hey, what are you doing?

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: I'm not playing word games with you anymore. The fist talks louder!

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Alright, I won't charge you for the noodles. How about that?

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: Are you kidding me? You think one bowl of noodles is gonna do it?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Let... let me go, I can't breathe...

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: You heard him? Let him go!

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: And who do think you are? Go eat your noodles and stop poking your nose where it doesn't belong.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Didn't you hear him? Let. Him. Go.

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: Looks like you want a beating too, eh?

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: I... I'm sorry, it's all my fault, I won't do it again... please, let me go...

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Could you stop crying? You make it sound like I'm bullying you.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (I hit him harder than I meant to. I hope he's okay...)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Are you gonna be alright? Do you need a doctor?

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: (No way he really cares! He's making sure that I won't spill the beans on him!)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Are... you alright?

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: I-I'm fine, I just fell down on my own, nothing to do with you at all, not a thing!

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Er... fell down? I thought I...

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: No, you weren't even there, don't worry, it's all my fault for being so clumsy, haha...

steps.name: Hoodlum
steps.text: I-I gotta go, bye!

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: You're limping... just be careful, don't try to run too fast.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Thank you very much! Small businesses like ours always have a hard time.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: You're not hurt, are you?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Not at all, thanks to you.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Rumble—)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Er, sorry, but... are my noodles ready yet?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Oh, how silly of me! Take a seat, and I'll be right up with your order.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Thanks, kid. A certain little girl would've chewed my head off if I went home with soiled clothes.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: You have a daughter, sir?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Not exactly... well, I guess daughter's the best way to put it.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Oh? What do you mean?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: It's a long story... say, you have some good moves. Who did you study with?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: I'm nothing special, just learned a couple things from my dad.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I remember there was a guy who owned a security firm who used the same grappling technique. His surname escapes me at the moment...

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Ko. That's my father.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Yeah, that's it! How is he?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: He passed away last year.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Ah... I'm sorry to hear that.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: It's all in the past now, but thanks for the kind words.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Here's your noodles, sir. I added a bit of meat broth for you, a touch of extra flavor.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Oh... thank you.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Picks up chopsticks)

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Now...

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Puts down chopsticks) Is there something you wanted to say, sir?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Well, you know, rent around here is high, and businesses are always barely scraping by.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Yes, I know...

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Sure, chasing away that hoodlum was a big help, but you also made a mess of the place while you were at it.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: We ought to keep it separate, no? The noodles are for helping me out, which is one thing.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: And the other?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: About the mess you made... surely it's fair to ask that you pay for repairs?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Tightens fist) I was only trying to help you...

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Hey now, what's with the fist?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: You're gonna punch me? Looks like you're no better than that hoodlum, pushing people around just because you know kung fu.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: No... I didn't mean to...

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Then pay up!

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Sir, you shouldn't do this... it's not right...

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: What do you mean not right? Break something, pay for it. It's the proper way to do things.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: You only took a couple of bites, dad... you're not gonna get better like this.

steps.name: Sickly Man
steps.text: Oh, don't you worry. The guy in the next bed over already laughs at me for how over-protective my son is... *cough*, *cough*.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Well, you shouldn't laugh with him, the way your lungs are. Anything else you want to eat? I can slice another apple for you. Hard to sleep on an empty stomach, after all.

steps.name: Sickly Man
steps.text: It's been a long time since I've had fried rice.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Not sure that's a good idea. It'll give you indigestion and keep you up all night.

steps.name: Sickly Man
steps.text: Worrying again. I was just kidding, Fine, fine, slice me up an apple.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Sickly Man
steps.text: How's working coming along? Has Old Li been yelling at you?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: It's going great. Uncle Li says I've got a great attitude.

steps.name: Sickly Man
steps.text: Who do you think you're fooling? That long look on your face, I bet you got a good chewing out. No need to hide things from your dad, tell me the truth.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Well... I got into an argument with Uncle Li. It's just not fair for him to mistreat his customers like that over a few coins.

steps.name: Sickly Man
steps.text: Sigh, you're just like me, always so stubborn about doing the right thing. I paid my price; don't be like me.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Why do you say that? You've always taught me right and wrong.

steps.name: Sickly Man
steps.text: And look where it got me! You're barely twenty, with your whole life ahead of you. No need to get yourself bruised and battered like me.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: What are you talking about, dad?!

steps.name: Sickly Man
steps.text: Listen to your father, Hei-sing. Sometimes, you have to let it go rather than banging your head against it forever.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Daydreaming, kid? Like I said, the bill's fifteen thousand. How do you want to pay?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Loosens fist)

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: ...I don't have a lot of money on me. Can I pay it by helping out around the shop?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Ha, sure, wouldn't hurt to have some free labor. I'm sure you can put those muscles to use washing dishes. Meals and bed not included, just to be clear.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I'm done eating. I'll leave the cash here.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Thank you! Have a pleasant day, sir.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Oh, you said you wanted my thoughts, didn't you? Actually, I just found a big problem that I'd better share.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Appreciate it, sir, but I'm a little busy right now.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Sure, I can wait. Not sure if you can though.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Er... well, what is it, sir?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I was counting your fire extinguishers here while I was eating. I saw three.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: But if I'm not mistaken, we got some new regs last month that require a minimum of six for an establishment of this size, with a five thousand dollar fine per missing piece.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Let me run the numbers here real quick... comes out to fifteen thousand.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: The fire department's really cracking down on this stuff lately. One call, and the fire marshal's here in minutes. I do wonder if you'd have the time to sort things out.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: That sure is a pickle, isn't it?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: No need to beat around the bush, sir.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Given that you just opened, I think you should probably let it go. Trouble's bad for business.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: So you're here to play nice guy, eh? Don't you have better things to do than stick your nose where it doesn't belong?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Oh, but I think my nose very much belongs here. Fire safety is the responsibility of each and every Lungmen citizen, after all.

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: You... how dare you...?

steps.name: Noodle Shop Owner
steps.text: Fine, fine, whatever! Forget it, just get out, both of you!

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: You heard the man. Let's go.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Thank you so much for helping me out, sir. I'm not sure how to repay your kindness, but if you ever need a pair of strong hands, I'm happy to help.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Ha, don't mention it. All I did was say a few words.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: S-Sir!

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Really, there's no need to thank me.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: N-No, it's not that.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Is there something else?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Could you... could you teach me?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Teach you? What could I possibly teach you?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: I used to believe that right and wrong were as clear as black and white.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: But now, thinking back on things, I see only gray; where white ends and black starts, I just can't tell.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Oh? And why is that?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: There are so many people here in Lungmen. People looking for money, for justice, for life, for fun, for fame, for the truth... they all gather here.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Everyone has a different story, and everyone has their own ideas of right and wrong.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: When one person's right is another's wrong, they resort to violence and force their ideas on each other.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: What's right and wrong? Where's justice and fairness?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Teach me what you know, sir. I don't want to keep banging my head until I bleed, but I also don't want to bow down to anyone.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: You're still young. It's natural you feel lost.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: But I can't teach you what you want to know...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: I'm just one of the many people here in Lungmen, after all.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Sir, I...

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: (Rumble—)

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: ...But maybe I can teach you something else. Like how to make fried rice that tastes just right.

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: Fried rice?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Yeah. How about it?

steps.name: Hung
steps.text: I... Yes. Thank you, sir.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Let's go, then. We can get some spring onions and eggs from the market on the way.
